entry: Extinct archaic human species of the [[Pleistocene]], spanning nearly 2 million years. It was the first human species to evolve a humanlike body plan and gait, to leave Africa and colonize Asia and Europe. Some populations were ancestors of later human species, including *Homo heidelbergensis*. It was first described in 1893 by Eugène Dubois from a skullcap, molar and femur found on [[Java]], Indonesia. Reconstructed adults ranged from 141–167 cm (4 ft 8 in – 5 ft 6 in) in height and weighed about 50 kg (110 lb). East Asian populations averaged a brain volume of 1,000 cc (61 cu in). The species invented the Acheulean tool industry and is usually characterized as the first [[Hunter-gatherer|hunter-gatherer]]. Its last known occurrence is 108,000 to 117,000 years ago, in Southeast Asia.

Extinct small archaic human species from the Indonesian island of Flores, also called Flores Man. Remains of an individual who would have stood about 1.1 m (3 ft 7 in) tall were found in 2003 at Liang Bua cave. Its small body size is now generally accepted as the result of insular dwarfism, a common phenomenon among island animals. The species is thought to have survived until the arrival of modern humans about 50,000 years ago.

Extinct archaic human species from the Early Pleistocene of East and [[South Africa]]. The name means handy man. It lived from about 2.4 million to 1.65 million years ago, making it among the oldest known archaic humans. It manufactured the Oldowan stone tool industry and used its tools mainly for butchering. Early Homo is generally thought to have consumed high quantities of meat, and this species scavenged it. Its brain volume generally ranged from 500 to 900 cm³ (31–55 cu in). Its body proportions are known from only two highly fragmentary skeletons, and it may have been at least partly arboreal, like the [[Australopithecus|australopithecines]]. It coexisted with *Homo rudolfensis*, *Homo erectus* and *Paranthropus boisei*.

Disputed archaic human species of the Middle Pleistocene, known from Europe and Africa and possibly Asia. Otto Schoetensack named it in 1908 from the Mauer jawbone, found in a sand pit southeast of Heidelberg, Germany. Scholars disagree whether the species was the last common ancestor of modern humans, [[Neanderthal|Neanderthals]] and [[Denisovan|Denisovans]], or a separate lineage. Populations dispersed into Europe by 700,000 years ago, spreading Late Acheulean stone tools, and settlements became more permanent by 500,000 years ago.

Branch of mathematics concerned with [[Homology (mathematics)|homology]] in a general algebraic setting. Its origins lie in investigations in combinatorial topology and abstract algebra at the end of the 19th century, chiefly by [[Henri Poincaré]] and [[David Hilbert]]. Its development was closely intertwined with the emergence of [[Category theory|category theory]]. A central concept is that of chain complexes, which are studied through their homology and cohomology, and a spectral sequence is a powerful tool for extracting information from them. The subject has played an enormous role in [[Algebraic topology]] and has expanded into [[Commutative algebra]], [[Algebraic geometry]], [[Representation theory]] and the theory of partial differential equations. K-theory draws on its methods.

Algebraic structure associated with a [[Topological space|topological space]]. The term, originally introduced in [[Algebraic topology]], has three closely related usages. The first is the homology of a chain complex, a sequence of [[Abelian group|abelian groups]] whose homology groups are regarded as fundamental invariants of the complex. Homology theories associate a chain complex to another mathematical object and take its homology, examples being singular homology, Morse homology and Hochschild homology. Under suitable conditions, distinct homology theories applied to one topological space give the same groups, allowing a single homology of that space to be defined. This notion is closely related to ideas such as the holes of a surface or the cycles of a graph. The nth homology group is the quotient of cycles by boundaries, and [[Homological algebra]] relates the homology groups of different chain complexes.

Negative attitudes toward [[Homosexuality|homosexuality]] or toward people who identify, or are perceived, as lesbian, gay or bisexual. It has been described as contempt, prejudice, aversion or hatred, may be based on irrational fear, and is sometimes attributed to religious beliefs. It is observable in hostile behavior such as [[Discrimination|discrimination]] and violence. Recognized types include institutionalized homophobia, such as state-sponsored forms, and internalized homophobia, experienced by people with same-sex attractions. According to 2010 Hate Crimes Statistics from the FBI, 19.3 percent of hate crimes across the United States were motivated by a sexual orientation bias. The term was coined by psychologist George Weinberg in the 1960s. Professor David A. F. Haaga says that contemporary usage covers a wide range of negative emotions and behaviors, which does not fit the accepted definition of a [[Phobia|phobia]] as an intense, illogical or abnormal fear.

Romantic or sexual attraction between people of the same sex or gender, and the identity based on it. It is one of three main categories of [[Sexual orientation|sexual orientation]], along with [[Bisexuality|bisexuality]] and [[Heterosexuality|heterosexuality]]. Scientists favor biological explanations, especially prenatal hormonal effects on the fetal brain, and there is no conclusive evidence that parenting or early childhood experience plays a significant role. Research shows that it is a natural and normal variation in human sexuality, and major mental health organizations overwhelmingly reject conversion therapy as ineffective and potentially harmful. Domestic [[Sheep|sheep]] are the only conclusively documented nonhuman animals with exclusive same-sex orientation, although same-sex behavior occurs in many species. Homosexual relationships and acts have been admired and condemned throughout recorded history. Since the end of the 20th century, a global movement has sought freedom and equality for gay people, including marriage equality and equal ability to serve in the [[Military|military]].

Continuous deformation between two [[Continuous function|continuous functions]]. Two continuous functions from one [[Topological space|topological space]] to another are homotopic if one can be continuously deformed into the other, and such a deformation is a homotopy between them. Formally, a homotopy is a continuous function H from X × [0,1] to Y with H(x,0) = f(x) and H(x,1) = g(x) for all x in X. Homotopy is an [[Equivalence relation|equivalence relation]] on continuous functions, and its equivalence classes are called homotopy classes. A [[Torus|torus]] shaped like a doughnut can be continuously deformed into a coffee-mug shape. Homotopy groups and cohomotopy groups, important invariants in [[Algebraic topology]], are defined using homotopies.

Japanese multinational [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] and automotive manufacturer, headquartered in Tokyo. The company has been the world's largest [[Motorcycle|motorcycle]] manufacturer since 1959 and produces more than 14 million [[Internal combustion engine|internal combustion engines]] each year. It built and sold the Honda Super Cub, the most produced motor vehicle in history. In March 1986 it released Acura, the first dedicated luxury brand of any Japanese automaker. Its other products include garden equipment, marine engines, power generators and the HondaJet aircraft.

Republic in [[Central America]], bordered by [[Guatemala]], [[El Salvador]] and [[Nicaragua]]. Its capital and largest city is [[Tegucigalpa]]. Several Mesoamerican cultures, most notably the Maya, flourished there before Spanish colonization in the 16th century, and the Spanish introduced Catholicism and the Spanish language. Honduras became independent in 1821 and has since been a republic, though it has endured much social strife and political instability. Its economy is primarily agricultural and vulnerable to [[Natural disaster|natural disasters]] such as Hurricane Mitch in 1998. In 2022, according to the National Institute of Statistics, 73% of the population lived in poverty. A 2009 military coup toppled the government of Manuel Zelaya, and claims of electoral fraud followed the 2013 and 2017 presidential elections. Xiomara Castro was elected in 2021, and Nasry Asfura won the 2025 election amid claims of fraud and of electoral interference by the United States.

Sweet, viscous foodstuff made by several species of bees, the best known of which are [[Honey bee|honey bees]]. Bees gather the sugary secretions of plants, mainly floral nectar, and refine them through regurgitation, enzymatic activity and water evaporation in the hive. Honey is sweet because of its high concentrations of [[Fructose|fructose]] and [[Glucose|glucose]], and it has about the same relative sweetness as [[Sucrose|sucrose]]. One standard tablespoon (14 mL) provides around 180 kilojoules (43 kilocalories) of food energy. Its high sugar concentration and acidic pH mean that many [[Microorganism|microorganisms]] cannot grow in it, so properly stored honey does not spoil. Cave paintings in Cuevas de la Araña, [[Spain]], depict people foraging for honey at least 8,000 years ago. The husbandry of bees is known as [[Beekeeping|beekeeping]].

Mammal, the sole living member of the subfamily Mellivorinae within the [[Mustelidae]], also known as the ratel. It is widely distributed across [[Africa]], Southwest Asia and the [[Indian subcontinent]]. Its genus name, *Mellivora*, derives from [[Latin]] and means honey eater. The species name refers to the [[Cape of Good Hope]], where its type specimen was discovered. Adults measure 55 to 77 cm (22 to 30 in) long and weigh up to 16 kg (35 lb), with males larger than females. Its loose skin lets it turn freely within it, and it has an eversible anal pouch. Primarily carnivorous and solitary, it has few natural predators because of its thick skin and ferocious defenses. Females typically bear one to two cubs after a gestation of 50–70 days. Listed as least concern by the IUCN, it is best known in popular media as aggressive and fearless.

Eusocial flying insect of the genus *Apis*, the bee clade most familiar to humans. Honey bees build perennial nests in cavities, with hexagonal cells of secreted wax, and store surplus carbohydrate as [[Honey|honey]]. The best-known species is the [[Western honey bee|western honey bee]] (*Apis mellifera*), which was domesticated for honey production and crop [[Pollination|pollination]]. Native to mainland Afro-Eurasia, honey bees have been introduced to the Americas and Australia since the [[Age of Discovery]]. Beeswax is used in [[Candle|candles]], soap and cosmetics, and royal jelly and venom are used in [[Alternative medicine|alternative medicine]].

Large and diverse family, Meliphagidae, of small to medium-sized [[Passerine|passerine]] birds. It comprises 195 species in 51 genera, roughly half of them native to [[Australia]], with many others in [[New Guinea]]. Honeyeaters also occur in [[New Zealand]] and on Pacific islands as far east as Samoa and Tonga. Many have brush-tipped tongues for taking nectar, and many also eat insects or fruit. Many Australian plants, particularly in the Proteaceae, Myrtaceae and Ericaceae, are pollinated by honeyeaters. Although they resemble [[Sunbird|sunbirds]] and [[Hummingbird|hummingbirds]] in habit, they are not closely related, and the similarities are the consequence of convergent evolution.

Family of 16 bird species in the order Piciformes, also called indicator birds or honey birds. Its Old World tropical range is greatest in [[Africa]], with two species in [[Asia]]. Honeyguides are best known for guiding humans to [[Bee|bee]] colonies, with one or two species deliberately leading people to hives. The people take the honey, and the birds feed on the grubs and beeswax left behind. In northern [[Tanzania]], the species partner with Hadza hunter-gatherers, and the birds' help has been shown to raise the rate of finding bee colonies by 560%. Some experts believe that this cooperation dates back to [[Homo erectus]], about 1.9 million years ago. Interactions between honeyguides and [[Honey badger|honey badgers]] have also been reported, although videos of them have been accused of being staged.

International airport on the island of Chek Lap Kok. Opened in 1998 to replace Kai Tak Airport, it is the world's busiest cargo gateway and one of its busiest passenger airports. It has three runways, each 3.8 km (2.4 mi) long, and runs 24 hours a day. It handled 49.9 million international passengers in 2024, the 9th busiest airport in the world by international passenger traffic. It became the world's busiest airport by cargo traffic in 2010. [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]] and [[United Airlines]] use it as a stopover, and it employed about 60,000 people at the start of 2024.

Founding emperor of the [[Qing dynasty]] and second khan of the Later Jin. He consolidated the empire his father [[Nurhaci]] had founded and laid the groundwork for the conquest of the [[Ming dynasty]], although he died before it was accomplished. He conquered [[Inner Mongolia]] and the rest of [[Manchuria]] and invaded Korea, which became a Qing tributary state. In 1635 he changed the name of the Jurchens to Manchu, and in 1636 he renamed the dynasty from Great Jin to Great Qing. His reign names were Tiancong, from 1627 to 1636, and Chongde, from 1636 to 1643. It is unclear whether Hong Taiji was a title or a personal name, and the name is also rendered Huang Taiji.

Chinese revolutionary and religious leader who led the [[Taiping Rebellion]] against the [[Qing dynasty]]. Born into a Hakka family in [[Guangzhou]], he claimed mystical visions after repeatedly failing the imperial examinations, and came to believe that [[Jesus]] was his elder brother. He rejected [[Confucianism]] and propagated a fusion of Christianity, Daoism and millenarianism. In January 1851 he organized a rebel army and proclaimed the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, with himself as its Heavenly King. Taiping forces captured [[Nanjing]] in March 1853 and renamed it Tianjing. In 1856 he engineered the murder of his fellow leader Yang Xiuqing, and the purge that followed reached further Taiping leaders. The kingdom later lost ground to Qing advances.

Founding emperor of the [[Ming dynasty]] of China, reigning from 1368 to 1398. Born Zhu Yuanzhang into a peasant family in Anhui, he lost his parents and brother in an epidemic and briefly lived as a [[Buddhism|Buddhist]] novice monk. In 1352 he joined the Red Turban rebels, who sought to overthrow the Mongol-led [[Yuan dynasty]], and he captured [[Nanjing]] in 1356. He declared himself King of Wu in 1364 and in 1368 renamed the kingdom Da Ming, meaning Great Radiance. His era name, Hongwu, means Vastly Martial. His forces drove out the Mongol armies loyal to the Yuan dynasty and unified the country, but he failed to conquer Mongolia. Under his rule Ming China grew and recovered from prolonged wars, and he was succeeded by his grandson, the Jianwen Emperor.

City (pop., 2020: 350,964), capital of the U.S. state of [[Hawaii]]. Honolulu has been the capital since 1845, first of the independent Hawaiian Kingdom, then of a U.S. territory and, since 1959, of the state. Its harbor has long made it important as a Pacific port, and it hosts a major U.S. Navy base. The attack by the [[Empire of Japan]] on nearby Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941 prompted U.S. entry into [[World War II]]. Its tropical climate and beaches make it a major tourist destination, but since the start of the 21st century [[Climate change]] has contributed to [[Drought|drought]], water shortages and sea level rise.

French novelist and playwright. His novel sequence *La Comédie humaine*, a panorama of post-[[Napoleon|Napoleonic]] French life, is generally viewed as his magnum opus. His keen observation of detail and unfiltered portrayal of society make him one of the founders of [[Realism (arts)|realism]] in European literature. His characters are complex and morally ambiguous, and the city of Paris takes on human qualities in his fiction. His writing influenced [[Émile Zola]], [[Charles Dickens]], [[Marcel Proust]], [[Gustave Flaubert]], [[Henry James]] and [[Fyodor Dostoevsky]]. Many of his works have been made into films, and James called him the father of the novelists who followed.

Quality of worthiness and respectability, expressed as a code of conduct. Honor is both a social teaching and a personal ethos, with elements such as valor, [[Chivalry|chivalry]], honesty and compassion. It affects the social standing and self-evaluation of an individual or institution, such as a family, school, regiment or nation. In his 1755 dictionary, [[Samuel Johnson]] defined honor first as nobility of soul, magnanimity and a scorn of meanness. Honor is distinguished from [[Dignity|dignity]], which is measured against conscience rather than community judgment. In the early medieval period, a lord's honor was the group of manors or lands he held. Honor has declined in importance in the modern West, where [[Conscience|conscience]] and the [[Rule of law|rule of law]] have largely replaced it. It remains important in the [[Military|military]] and in [[Scouting]] organizations, which hold courts of honor.

Largest of the four main islands of [[Japan]]. It lies between the [[Pacific Ocean]] to the east and the [[Sea of Japan]] to the west, and is the seventh-largest island in the world and the second most populous after [[Java]]. It had a population of 100.7 million in 2025, or 81.9% of Japan's total, concentrated on coastal plains. About 30% of residents live in the Greater [[Tokyo]] area. Former capitals on the island include [[Kyoto]], Nara and Kamakura. Its highest peak is [[Mount Fuji]], at 3,776 m (12,388 ft), and its largest lake is Lake Biwa. Mountainous and volcanic, the island experiences frequent earthquakes, including the Great Kantō earthquake of 1923 and the 2011 earthquake that caused devastating tsunamis.

Single- or multi-stemmed water pipe for smoking [[Tobacco|tobacco]], flavored tobacco or sometimes [[Cannabis (drug)|cannabis]]. The hookah was invented by Abul-Fath Gilani, an Iranian physician of [[Akbar]] in Fatehpur Sikri, Mughal India, and spread from the Indian subcontinent to Persia and the Ottoman Empire. Its name derives from the Hindustani word huqqa, of [[Arabic]] origin. Smoking through a hookah exposes users to toxic chemicals, carcinogens and heavy metals, and sharing pipes can transmit infectious disease. Its use is a [[Public health|public health]] concern, with high rates among young people in the United States and Europe.
